chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abi 'Abdillah, from his father, from 'Ali عليه السلام.
“That a virgin woman was brought to him, and they alleged that she had committed zina. So he ordered the women, and they looked at her and said: She is a virgin. Then he said:
'Ali عليه السلام said: “I would not strike one upon whom there is a seal from Allah, and he used to deem the testimony of women valid in the like of this.”

key_terms.خَاتَمٌ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ: a mark or seal from Allah, here referring to a divinely given sign of virginity
key_terms.لِأَضْرِبَ: to inflict the prescribed striking or punishment

ai.seo_question: Can the testimony of women be accepted in determining bodily matters in zina-related cases?
ai.summary: This report concerns a legal judgment in a zina case involving a virgin woman. Imam 'Ali عليه السلام refused to inflict punishment after women examined her and confirmed her virginity, indicating recognition of women’s testimony in such matters and caution in applying legal penalties.
